sprint: BACKLOG.md -- Add Image Option to Page Background (root Studio only)
task: Closes BACKLOG.md's bug line, verbatim: 'Add image option also in background.' The existing Personalize -> Page Background control (js/contextPanel.js's _appendBackground) only ever let a Story Author pick a flat colour for a page's background fill -- no way to use an uploaded picture instead. Added a Background Type toggle (Colour / Image, via the existing shared single-select _makeIconChoiceRow) right above the existing Colour Kit swatch row; picking Image reveals a new _appendBackgroundImageControls block -- an Upload/Replace Picture button (routed through the established _storeUploadedAsset per-module upload adapter, producing a durable vihu-asset: reference via AssetStore.put, falling back gracefully to a raw data: URI on any failure), a conditional 0-359 degree Rotation slider (via the existing _makeRangeRow, shown only once a picture is uploaded) and a Remove Picture button (new .context-btn-danger styling, mirroring the Selection Action Strip's own destructive-action red-tint convention) that clears the image and reverts the page to its prior/fallback colour fill. On the render side (renderer/slideRenderer.js), _slideBackgroundOverride now returns null whenever backgroundMode==='image' (so the old colour-fill code path correctly steps aside), a new _slideBackgroundImageOverride resolves {ref,rotation} off the override bag, and a new _drawSlideBackgroundImage paints the full-page picture via the existing _layerDrawDecorationImage helper, reusing its established cover-fit + rotation-around-centre math -- zero new drawing primitives invented. The two modes are strictly mutually exclusive at the model level (co.backgroundMode gates which fields are read), so a page always shows exactly one clear background source with no silent double-render. Verified end-to-end via a new, dedicated 26-assertion Playwright suite (bg_image_verify.js, scratch-only) driving the real UI -- a genuine native-file-chooser upload (not a synthetic call), the toggle switching Colour<->Image with the correct controls shown/hidden at each state, a real mouse-driven Rotation slider drag with before/after canvas pixel sampling confirming the picture visibly rotates, Remove Picture correctly reverting to the prior colour fill (pixel-sampled to confirm), and a full round trip back to Colour mode restoring the original swatch-driven fill -- all 26 checks passing, zero console/page errors. One test-script bug was found and fixed during this pass, not an app bug: three DOM queries in bg_image_verify.js used an exact-string match against a range-row label element (r.textContent==='Rotation'), but _makeRangeRow's label div always concatenates the plain label text with a second, live-updating value span as sibling children (e.g. the div's real textContent reads 'Rotation0deg', never bare 'Rotation') -- confirmed via direct code read of _makeRangeRow (js/contextPanel.js) that this concatenation is exactly how every other range row in this codebase already renders, not a bug; fixed the test's three query sites to use a starts-with prefix check instead. Full regression: museum_realfile_pixelhash.js (the real, on-disk themes/MuseumGallery.vtheme rendered end to end and SHA-256-hashed, producing the exact e7b2a905613dbef3d2f9064211103d84762d7039d3bee404df90f4d90899b390 hash this project's history has recorded repeatedly, confirming zero visual/rendering regression), verify_bg_zorder_fix.js and verify_transparent_bg.js (8/8, confirming the pre-existing background z-order/transparent-fill fallback logic sitting alongside the modified render loop is unaffected), icon_row_active_verify.js (59/59, confirming the shared single-select icon-row mechanism the new Background Type toggle reuses works correctly everywhere), and welcome_heading_removed_verify.js (4/4, confirming the Personalize default view / Context Panel structure is unaffected) all pass unchanged, zero console/page errors. No Theme Contract/Engine V2 Scene Model/Builder architecture change; confined to js/contextPanel.js, renderer/slideRenderer.js, and css/style.css.
